descriptionChirho: To take off or remove one's own clothing or outer garment (intransitive/reflexive Qal usage), including the Hitpael reflexive form.
To make a sudden military incursion, raid, or rush upon an enemy or territory.
To strip bare or despoil in a general sense (Qal transitive), including stripping bark or plundering goods.
To strip or plunder intensively, despoiling the slain or defeated (Piel intensive stem).
To causatively remove garments or armor from another person, to strip someone naked or bare.

labelChirho: Hifil: flay or skin an animal
descriptionChirho: To remove the skin or hide from a sacrificial animal, to flay (specialized Hifil usage in cultic contexts).
